mentions.text: The integration of realtime data, such as recent user actions, results in more accurate recommendations and increases the probability of users discovering relevant items (Chen et al., 2019; Pi et al., 2020).
To address this challenge, some approaches have utilized hashing and nearest neighbor search in long user sequences (Pi et al., 2020).
Other work encodes users’ past actions over an extended time frame to a user embedding (Pancha et al., 2022) to represent long-term user interests.
For user actions that occur over an extended period of time, we transform them into a batch user representation (Pancha et al., 2022).
We demonstrate that combining TransAct with daily-generated user representations (Pancha et al., 2022) to a hybrid model leads to the best performance in Pinnability.
Collaborative filtering (CF) (Sarwar et al., 2001; Ma et al., 2007; Jin et al., 2004) makes recommendations based on the assumption that a user will prefer an item that other similar users prefer.
Factorization machines (Rendle, 2010a; Rendle, 2010b), on the other hand, are able to handle sparse matrices.
For example, Google uses Wide & Deep (Cheng et al., 2016) models for application recommendation.
DeepFM (Guo et al., 2017) makes improvements by learning both low-order and high-order feature interactions automatically.
DCN (Wang et al., 2017) and its upgraded version DCN v2 (Wang et al., 2021) both aim to automatically model the explicit feature crosses.
We are inspired by the previous sequential recommendation method (Chen et al., 2019) in terms of encoding users’ past action into a dense representation.

Some early sequential recommendation systems use machine learning techniques, such as Markov Chain (He and McAuley, 2016) and session-based K nearest neighbors (KNN) (Hu et al., 2020) to model the temporal dependencies among interactions in users’ action history.

Recently, deep learning techniques such as recurrent neural networks (RNN) (Schuster and Paliwal, 1997) have shown great success in natural language processing and have become increasingly popular in sequential recommendation.
As a result, many DL-based sequential models (Donkers et al., 2017; Hidasi et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2019) have achieved outstanding performance using RNNs.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) (Zhao et al., 2017) are widely used for processing time-series data and image data.

In the context of sequential recommendation, CNN-based models can effectively learn dependency within a set of items users recently interacted with, and make recommendations accordingly (Tang and Wang, 2018; Tuan and Phuong, 2017).
Attention mechanism is originated from the neural machine translation task, which models the importance of different parts of the input sentences on the output words (Bahdanau et al., 2014).
Self-attention is a mechanism known to weigh the importance of different parts of an input sequence (Vaswani et al., 2017).
There have been more recommender systems that use attention (Zhou et al., 2018) and self-attention (Zhang et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2019; Li et al., 2020; Kang and McAuley, 2018; Sun et al., 2019a).
Many previous works (Kang and McAuley, 2018; Li et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2019a) only perform offline evaluations using public datasets.
Alibaba’s Behavior Sequence Transformer (BST) (Chen et al., 2019) is the improved version of DIN and is closely related to our work.
The high-level architecture is a Wide and Deep learning (WDL) model (Cheng et al., 2016).
We then apply a feature cross using a full-rank DCN V2 (Wang et al., 2021) to explicitly model feature interactions.

As shown in Figure 2, our model is a realtime-batch hybrid model that encodes the user action history features by both realtime (TransAct) and batch (PinnerFormer) approaches and optimizes for the ranking task (Xu et al., 2022).
For each action, we use three primary features: the timestamp of the action, action type, and the 32-dimensional PinSage embedding (Ying et al., 2018) of the pin.
As mentioned earlier, the content of pins in the user action sequence is represented by PinSage embeddings (Ying et al., 2018).
• append: Append candidate pin’s PinSage embedding to user action sequence as the last entry of the sequence, similar to BST (Chen et al., 2019).

Some popular model architectures for sequential modeling in the industry include CNN(Zhao et al., 2017), RNN (Schuster and Paliwal, 1997) and recently transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017), etc. We experimented with different sequence aggregation architectures and choose transformer-based architectures.
Since the output is compact enough, it can be easily integrated into the Pinnability framework using the DCN v2 (Wang et al., 2021) feature crossing layer.
Without retraining, a recommender system’s performance can degrade as the user’s behavior and preferences change, leading to less accurate recommendations (Sculley et al., 2015).
However, for GPU-based inference, larger batches are more efficient (Sze et al., 2017).
The application then materializes the features and stores them in Rockstore (Chan, 2022).
We use an Adam (Kingma and Ba, 2015) optimizer with a learning rate scheduler.
This is also referred to as the cold-start user problem in recommendation (Natarajan et al., 2020).
The first baseline is the WDL model (Cheng et al., 2016) that incorporates sequence features as part of its wide features.
The second baseline is Alibaba’s behavior sequence transformer (BST) model (Chen et al., 2019).
We opted not to compare our results with DIN (Zhou et al., 2018) as BST has already demonstrated its superiority over DIN.
Additionally, we did not compare with variants like BERT4Rec (Sun et al., 2019b) as the problem formulations are different and a direct comparison is not feasible.

TransAct captures users’ immediate interests, which contribute the most to the user’s overall engagement, while PinnerFormer (PF) (Pancha et al., 2022) extracts users’ long-term preferences from their historical behavior.
LSTM: use Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber, 1997), a more sophisticated version of RNN that better captures longer-term dependencies by using memory cells and gating.
